Address.description:
A position in a language's namespace: the package it belongs to and the
path within it — `fff :: [grep, types]` for a Rust module, path
components for a TypeScript file. Prefix relations, which are what a move
cares about, never hold across packages.

ImportGroup.description:
Where a grouped entry sits, so a surgery can rewrite it in place or move
it out of the group.

item.description: The whole entry, alias or nested list included (`parse::Config as Cfg`).

items.description: How many entries that list has.

list.description: The innermost list the entry belongs to, braces included.

prefix.description: Combined prefix of the enclosing groups (`crate::util`).

top_level.description: Whether `list` is the statement's own list rather than a nested one.

ImportSite.description: One path in one file. `span` covers exactly the text a rewrite replaces.

alias.description:
The name the statement binds instead of the path's last segment:
`Cfg` in `use a::Config as Cfg`.

declares.description:
Part of an import statement (`use`, `import`), so it brings its last
segment into the file's scope. A qualified path in an expression
(`fff::GrepMatch` in a type position) is a reference to rewrite on a
move, but declares nothing.

glob.description: `use a::b::*`: every name under the path is brought into scope.

group.description:
Present when the path is an entry of a grouped import such as
`use a::{b, c::d}`; replacing `span` alone can then only express
paths that stay under the group's prefix.

path.description:
The full path as written (`crate::a::b`, `../x/y`), parsed by the
grammar's [`PathSyntax`]. For a grouped entry this includes the
group's prefix.

reexport.description:
A `pub use`, an `export … from`: the name it brings in is offered on
again under this file's address, so a path to it here reaches the
original declaration.

ModulePath.description:
A path as spelled in source: its head and its segments, with the syntax
that spells it. Serialises as the text, so the wire is what the user
wrote.

Name.description: One identifier: a module, a declaration, a file stem. Compared by text.

PackageId.description:
The name a package goes by in paths: a Rust crate's lib name (`fff`, not
`fff-search`), a TypeScript package's name. The layout decides the spelling.

Position.description:
Zero-based line and character column. Columns count `char`s, not bytes,
so they are safe to show to humans and editors.

RelPath.description:
A file's path inside the workspace, spelled the way the project does: `/`
on every platform.

A workspace path is a project path — like a `mod` path or a
`crate::a::b` address — not a path of the machine, so it carries its own
spelling and is what goes on the wire, into a row, or into a diagnostic.
It reads as a [`Path`] (an OS path is made from one at the edge, where a
file is actually read), but it cannot spell a separator the host's way:
`Display`, serde and the stored bytes are always `/`.

Span.description: Half-open byte range `[start, end)` inside a single file.

description:
`imports [path]`: import statements worth a look — unused, unresolved,
or the same target twice.

path.description: The file asked about; every file when absent.

redundant.description:
Declared imports naming an address another statement in the file
already brings in.

unplaced.description:
Files whose language has a layout but which it cannot place — a
crate's integration tests, say — so their imports were not judged.

unresolved.description: Declared imports the layout could not place.

unused.description: Declared imports whose bound name the file never spells again.
